::: {#rem-reproducibility}

#### Seeds are not enough

PyTorch's documentation warns that completely reproducible results are not guaranteed
across PyTorch releases or platforms,
or between a CPU and a GPU,
even with identical seeds [@pytorch_randomness].
Some GPU operations are nondeterministic,
and `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` makes PyTorch choose deterministic ones,
often more slowly,
or raise an error where it has none [@pytorch_randomness].
So record more than the seed:
the [hyperparameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/model-selection.html#sec-hyperparameters),
the versions of the code, the data and the libraries,
and the trained weights themselves.
[lds's section on tracking runs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/ml-experimentation.html#tracking-runs) gives the habits that make a result traceable a month later. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

:::
